I can confirm the same crash pattern on Windows after upgrading to OpenCode 1.17.10.

Environment, sanitized:
- OS: Windows 11 x64
- OpenCode install: npm global
- Crashing OpenCode version: 1.17.10
- Embedded Bun shown in crash output: v1.3.14 (0d9b296a), Windows x64 baseline standalone executable
- Workaround: downgrading to opencode-ai@1.17.9 appears stable so far under the same general workflow

Common crash signature:

```text
Bun v1.3.14 (0d9b296a) Windows x64 (baseline)
Windows v.win11_dt
panic(main thread): Segmentation fault
oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.
```

I saw the crash multiple times in different UI states, not just one action:

1. Immediately after pasting a GitHub issue URL into the input box.
2. During a session while OpenCode was reading/searching files and the LSP panel showed TypeScript activity.
3. After displaying a normal verification/result message in the TUI.
4. After showing a config diff in the TUI.

This makes it look less like a specific prompt, provider, SQLite DB, or LSP-only issue, and more like a Windows standalone/Bun runtime regression exposed through the TUI/native layer in 1.17.10.

Additional note: I initially suspected a mixed-version state because an older OpenCode instance had been left open. After fully restarting and confirming only 1.17.10 instances were running, the crash still reproduced. Downgrading to 1.17.9 is the only thing that has stopped the fatal crash so far.

I have also observed this behavior for copilot opus 4.8 model in opencode. The model keep emits a 'call' token repeatedly even in successful tool calls and eventually failed for calling tools or only emits this `call` token in response. May I ask are there any updates for this?

### Bun segfault crash under parallel tool calls in long TUI sessions

### 环境 (Environment)

- **opencode 版本**: v1.17.10
- **Bun 版本**: 1.3.14
- **操作系统**: Windows 10.0.26200 x64
- **终端**: PowerShell 7.6.2 (Core)
- **会话类型**: CLI TUI
- **Session ID (ses_1033)**: `ses_1033c1af1ffeGUoXROOsp9UQyr` — 4 次崩溃
- **Session ID (ses_1031)**: `ses_1031fbd38ffelYtm1hQNtQ8u7B` — 第 5 次复现（新会话）

### 复现步骤 (Steps to reproduce)

1. 在 CLI TUI 中启动 opencode 会话
2. 通过 `/session-start` 恢复之前的长期会话（上下文 >80K tokens）
3. 密集发起并行 tool calls（read / bash / grep / glob，每次 2-3 个并行）
4. 观察 Bun 进程 segfault 崩溃

> 触发条件：并行 tool calls + 上下文约 80K–100K+ tokens。串行调用或短会话（<50K tokens）未复现此问题。跨会话验证：即使话题内容不同（根因排查 vs 文档整理），相同触发条件仍稳定复现。

### 预期行为 (Expected behavior)

进程持续运行，不因内存压力 segfault。

### 实际行为 (Actual behavior)

Bun 1.3.14 在 Windows 上 segfault，进程无征兆终止，无 JavaScript 异常捕获。

### 崩溃数据 (Crash Data)

同一 session 内 30 分钟崩溃 4 次（ses_1033），第 5 次在后续新会话中复现（ses_1031）：

| # | 会话 | 时间 | 进程寿命 | 触发场景 | 内存状态 |
|---|------|------|---------|---------|---------|
| C1 | ses_1033 | ~11:13 | ~16min | 前序会话的并行 tool calls | Rss 0.90GB / Peak 1.03GB / Faults 1,006,743 / 960,776ms |
| C2 | ses_1033 | 11:32 | ~18min | vision subagent + 文件编辑 | Rss 1.00GB / Peak 1.20GB / Faults 2,212,204 / 1,096,343ms |
| C3 | ses_1033 | 11:36 | ~3min | 文件编辑 + learning 记录更新 | 无截图，用户确认 |
| C4 | ses_1033 | 11:42 | ~1min | 密集并行 tool calls（read+bash+grep+glob） | 上下文 100K→106K tokens |
| C5 | ses_1031 | 12:24 | ~40min | 高上下文下单次文件写入（上下文 134K tokens） | Rss 1.00GB / Peak 1.10GB / Faults >2M |

**间隔（ses_1033 内）**: 16min → 18min → 3min → 1min。上下文基线：11K → 106K tokens。

**跨会话（C5）**: 新会话 ses_1031，上下文 134K tokens 时崩溃。

**C4 最后一次并行批次**:

```
11:41:17  read     (LEARNINGS.md)
11:41:18  bash     (Get-ChildItem skills)
11:41:18  grep     (pattern search)
         ─── 3 parallel ───
11:41:22  glob     (*.md)
11:41:22  bash     (git log -5)
11:41:22  glob     (**/*.ts)
         ─── 3 parallel ───
11:41:26  bash     (Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter *.ts)
11:41:26  read     (SKILL.md)
11:41:26  bash     (git diff --stat)
         ─── 3 parallel (2 running) ───
→ 11:42:36  segfault
```

@zcutlip You're right, and I want to make sure your work here isn't lost. Your comments in this thread were the most thorough tracing of this problem — the source-code spelunking into how skills work internally, the distinction between slash-command invocation vs. the skill tool, the observation about missing `<skill_content>` context in the command path, and the `{CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` gap — all of that was essential to understanding why #33580 only fixed part of the problem.

I've opened #33786 to capture the two remaining bug code paths you and @micha149 identified:
1. The system prompt `<available_skills>` block still URL-encodes `<location>` (same `pathToFileURL` bug, second occurrence)
2. Skills invoked as slash commands get no directory context at all — just raw SKILL.md content with no base directory or file list

PR #33787 fixes both.

The third issue you raised — the lack of a deterministic `${SKILL_ROOT}` macro (or equivalent) for skill authors to reliably reference bundled files — is a design-level feature request. That one needs the OpenCode team to weigh in on the approach, so it belongs in a separate feature discussion rather than a bug fix PR. I'd encourage you to open that one if you haven't already, since you've clearly thought through the design tradeoffs already.

Closing this. The linked issue #33092 was closed as not-planned, so under the issue-first policy the standards bot keeps flagging this PR as having no valid linked issue. The change stands on its own merit (aligns `Bom.split()` with the existing `splitBom()` in `packages/core/src/file-mutation.ts`), so if a maintainer wants to pick it up later the diff and tests are here. Closing to keep the queue clean — happy to reopen if anyone wants to take it.

**Re: the bot's note about #29429**

Worth clarifying since the bot framed them as "complementary" — for **bug 2 (slash-command skills lacking directory context)**, #29429 and this PR actually overlap on the same lines in `command/index.ts`, so they're alternative solutions rather than complementary:

- **#29429** sets the slash template to `""` and routes `source === "skill"` commands through `skill.execute(...)` in `session/prompt.ts`, producing the *full* skill context (including the ripgrep-sampled `<skill_files>` listing).
- **This PR** keeps it lightweight: it just appends the `Base directory` hint to the template, matching the `skill` tool's wording but without the file listing.

I went with the lightweight approach because it resolves the reported symptom (agent can't locate bundled `references/`/`scripts/`) with a minimal, self-contained change and no new execution path. If the maintainers prefer the richer file-listing behavior from #29429, bug 2 here can be dropped to avoid the conflict — but **bug 1 (the `pathToFileURL` URL-encoding of `<location>` in `Skill.fmt()`) is independent and not touched by #29429**, so that part stands on its own regardless.

I dug into the Windows Desktop v1.17.4 bundle and confirmed this is still a frontend rendering/propagation issue in addition to persistence/refresh behavior.

What changed in v1.17.4:
- The desktop app still stores project icon data in workspace stores (workspace:icon / workspace:project) as JSON-wrapped data URLs.
- The main renderer now has hashed bundles, but the sidebar/project list still needs to merge childStore.projectMeta?.icon?.override back into project.icon.override in every enrich path.
- The edit project dialog also needs to load the stored icon override so the preview survives restart/update.

I put together a workaround patch that adapts to hashed bundle filenames and is idempotent across updates:
- gist: https://gist.github.com/Bl0ck154/fa7d0b8cc900e6924e4f420da6bcb6fb
- raw patcher: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Bl0ck154/fa7d0b8cc900e6924e4f420da6bcb6fb/raw/patch-opencode-icons.mjs

If helpful, I can also summarize the exact bundle-level diff / matching blocks I found in v1.17.4.

Found a mistake in the issue description.

It says v1.17.10 **added** the `replacement_seq` column. It is the opposite — the migration **removes** it.

PR #33378 (the simplify refactor in v1.17.10) did three things together:
1. Added a migration: `DROP COLUMN replacement_seq`
2. Removed the column from the runtime schema
3. Removed the `requestReplacement` function entirely

So v1.17.10 is consistent with itself — the column is gone, and the code does not need it. No error on v1.17.10 alone.

**The error only happens when old code meets the new schema.** Two ways that can happen:

1. **You downgrade** — upgraded to 1.17.10, migration ran (column dropped), then went back to 1.17.9. Old `requestReplacement` still reads `replacement_seq`, column does not exist anymore. This is what the issue describes.

2. **Stale process** — e.g. an `opencode serve` daemon from before the upgrade is still running with old code. The new TUI sends `prompt_async` requests to it over HTTP. The daemon runs the old code, hits the deleted column, and fails. The error shows up in your TUI because it is the HTTP response coming back. This is what I ran into.
